fact: Space in Africa states NIPOST switched on the National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode on 1 October 2026, giving each captured addressable building an 11-character code.
Nairametrics reports the National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System launched through NIPOST on 1 October 2026, with users already finding 11-character building postcodes.
TheCable states the federal executive council approved the national digital addressing policy and digital postcode system in March 2026.
TheCable states NIPOST launched the national digital alphanumeric postcode system, assigning 11-character codes to addressable buildings, and its reporters used the application.

Tech Africa News says Nigeria introduced the National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System on 1 October 2026, led by NIPOST with Milsat Technologies, and that it assigns an 11-character code to every addressable building.

Tech Africa News says NDAPS assigns a code to every addressable building in the country and its database holds structures across the entire country, mapped from satellite imagery and field verification.

The Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation & Digital Economy says Nigeria has a National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System that identifies locations and properties, on which five builders pitched services on 27 October 2026.
TechCabal reports Nigeria's National Digital Addressing System (NDAPS), led by NIPOST, launched on October 1 with 11-character alphanumeric digital postcodes.

Technext reports NIPOST rolled out the National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System on 1 October 2026, assigning an 11-character GIS-enabled code to addressable buildings, with early users reporting mixed results.

The Nigerian Postal Service says Nigeria is introducing a new building-level alphanumeric postcode, with the postcode app and website scheduled to launch on 1 October 2026 and building owners able to request a code.

At a National Addressing Council meeting chaired by the Vice President, agencies ratified a preliminary framework to realise a digitised national addressing infrastructure, replacing the obsolete 2017 National Addressing Policy, BusinessDay reports.

The Federal Government has revived the national digital postcode project, fully federally funded for the first time, to give every standing building a unique GIS-enabled location identifier, and NIMC and NIPOST signed an MoU to integrate postcode retrieval into the NIN platform, which users will 'soon' be able to use (NIPOST Postmaster General and NIMC Director-General).
